text:
A: Hiya! Oh, you're the dog one!
B: Ha, the dog one, I'll take that. Alright? I'm Darren.
A: Ellie! I saw the lead on the hook in your photo. What's your dog called?
B: Biscuit. Border Terrier.
A: No way. Mine's called Biscuit! Well, my mum's. Fat old Staffie cross.
B: You're joking. Has yours eaten a sock?
A: Yes! A whole one, last week! We were proper worried, and then it just, like, came out the other end.
B: Ha, ours ate another one Monday, I'm still waiting on that. Where are you based, Ellie?
A: Barnstaple. North Devon.
B: Oh, lovely. We went Croyde a few years back with the dog. Stayed in a little place up the hill, had a pint at the Thatch every night.
A: Shut up, that's where I surf! Well, kind of surf. I'm decent on a foamie, I'm getting there on a proper board.
B: Better than me, mate. I stood up once for about a second and that was my lot. What d'you do for work, then? Leisure centre, is it?
A: Yeah, I'm a lifeguard, and I teach the kids' swimming lessons. How'd you know?
B: The hoodie, to be fair. And the other Darren in this group runs a leisure centre, in Taunton. Same as me. We worked out we've got loads in common.
A: Oh my god, is he the one with the polo shirt? I thought he looked exactly like my supervisor!
B: Ha, that'll be him. Nice bloke. Bit quieter than me.
A: Most people are quieter than me, so. What do you do?
B: I run a builders' merchant. Trade counter, yard, couple of drivers. We get students in over the summer on the counter, and honestly, you remind me of them. In a good way. Loads of energy, chatting to the builders.
A: Aw, that's nice! I love chatting to the regulars. There's this old man who comes in every morning at seven, does exactly twenty lengths, and tells me about his allotment. I know more about his runner beans than my own family.
B: That's the job though, innit. Half of mine's knowing what the builders are working on. I've got one been nearly finished on an extension for eight months.
A: Eight months! What's he building, a castle?
B: That's what I said! He just goes, "nearly there, Daz."
A: Ha! So, do you like, go away much? I'm saving for Australia. Working holiday, maybe in a couple of years.
B: Australia, good on you. Do it while you're young. I went Las Vegas for my fortieth with three mates. Lost about forty quid on the slots, but don't tell my partner.
A: That's so sick though. Did you get married by Elvis?
B: Ha, no! We've been together thirteen years and never got round to it. She'd kill me if I did it in Vegas without her.
A: You could take her back and do it! That'd be proper romantic.
